summary.text: Dometic FreshJet Series 4 (fixed-speed) and Series 7 (inverter) are 220-240 V roof air conditioners for caravans and RVs, run from a control panel or remote control. Faults show on the display as P or E codes listed in the troubleshooting table.

models.text: The manual covers four models: FJX4333EEH (FreshJet 4-Series, fixed-speed) and FJX7333IHP, FJX7337IHP and FJX7457IHP (FreshJet 7-Series, inverter).
Rated cooling capacity: 2200 W (FJX4333EEH), 2537 W (FJX7333IHP), 2910 W (FJX7337IHP), 3400 W (FJX7457IHP); heating 1000, 2285, 2692 and 2903 W.
Supply: 220-240 V / 50 Hz (FJX4333EEH) or 220-240 V / 50-60 Hz (7-Series); required fuse 10 A; rated cooling current under 6 A to under 7.8 A depending on model.
Operating ambient range is -2 C to 52 C; the unit is designed to be installed within plus or minus 10 degrees of horizontal, on roofs 25-60 mm thick (400 x 400 mm cutout).

display.text: The control panel display shows the set temperature and, while the fan is being adjusted, the fan level; separate symbols indicate air purifier active, degrees Celsius and timer set.
Fan speed Low, Med, High, Turbo or Auto shows briefly on the air distribution box display as 1, 2, 3, 4 or AA when changed.

Faults are reported as "The display shows:" a code: P codes (P0-P7, P9) for protection events and E codes (E0-EL) for sensor, drive and communication faults, each with a suggested remedy in the table.
The remote control display shows time, target temperature, actual room temperature, mode, fan speed, active-function symbols and battery status; the unit confirms each received command with a beep.

reset.text: The power button only toggles between on and standby; the roof air conditioner can be switched off only by cutting the power supply.
When switched back on, the unit resumes operation with the previously set values.
To cancel a preset timer, press the timer button once; the timer symbols disappear and preset values are discarded.

checks.text: Before first use, check that supply voltage and frequency match the technical data, and that air intake openings, air nozzles and all ventilation grilles are free.
Unit does not switch on: first check the power supply is connected; a voltage below 200 V means campsite power is not sufficient.

If the power-supply fuse is too low, the campsite supply is overloaded: check site power, unwind the cable drum if used, reduce active electrical consumers in the vehicle, and check the campsite electrical protection.
Regularly remove leaves and dirt from the air intake and ventilation grilles without damaging them; never use a high-pressure cleaner, petrol, diesel or solvents.
Regularly check that the condensation water drainage channels at the sides of the unit are clear so condensate can escape.
Regularly clean the air distribution box filters: pull them out with a flat screwdriver in the handle, wash in detergent solution, let dry, slide back in.
Once per year, check the seals between the roof air conditioner and the vehicle roof for cracks and other damage.

parts.text: Troubleshooting names temperature sensors, evaporator fan, condenser fan, voltage converter and roof seals as possible causes; for each the remedy is to contact an authorized service agent or Dometic.
The icing sensor trips when the outer temperature is too low or all air nozzles are closed, making the unit constantly switch itself off.

Code-table components: IPM module, compressor drive, discharge tube, evaporator and condenser coil sensors, room and outdoor sensors, current sensor, outdoor EEPROM, LIN-BUS/CI-BUS link; all routed to an authorized service agent or Dometic.
The heat exchanger is to be serviced once per year by a specialist company.
A damaged supply cord must be replaced by the manufacturer, its service agent or similarly qualified personnel.

callTech.text: Repair may only be carried out by qualified personnel familiar with the risks and regulations; for repair service contact the service center in your country (dometic.com/dealer). Always disconnect power when working on the appliance.

Anyone working on or breaking into the refrigerant circuit must hold a current valid refrigerant-handling certificate; faults in the refrigerant circuit must be checked and repaired by the manufacturer or its service agent.
The unit uses flammable R32 refrigerant, which may have no odor; never use ignition sources such as a halide torch to search for leaks.
Maintenance beyond the tasks described may only be done by qualified personnel familiar with refrigerant and air conditioning systems.
In a fire, do not undo the upper cover of the appliance and do not use water; use approved extinguishing agents.
For P0, P2, P4-P7, P9 and most E codes the table's only remedy is to contact an authorized service agent or Dometic; for P1, P3 and E9 first check campsite voltage with site management.
Warranty is 3 years; send a receipt copy and fault description. Self-repair or nonprofessional repair can have safety consequences and might void the warranty.
